propositions: Each of ~13,255 tests calls `git rev-parse HEAD` twice (before/after), consuming ~207 runner-seconds / 75 wall-seconds projected; eliminating per-test Git subprocesses would save ~9% wall time on the 895-test sample.
The current per-test guard must preserve exact checkout-HEAD attribution (naming the responsible test) and the allow_repo_writes escape hatch; session-level dirty-tree detection must remain enabled.

No consensus-safe implementation exists: adding a Git library (Dulwich/pygit2) increases dependency surface; hand-parsing symbolic/loose/packed/worktree/reftable refs is unsafe; removing the attribution guard weakens test fidelity relative to four surveyed OSS projects.

OSS consensus (4/4: pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit) rejects per-test source-checkout Git subprocesses in the hot path, but none maintains rebar's stricter per-test checkout-HEAD attribution contract.
